name: Eton Blue
lede: Eton Blue is a school color: the light blue of Eton, a public school in England, whose name was later shared with a university.

sections.title: The name
sections.body: Paterson's dictionary says Eton blue is the school's light blue, taken up in the 16th century and later borrowed by Cambridge University [1]. The same dictionary says the light blue Eton color became Cambridge blue after, it is said, a rower's mistake in the 1836 boat race against Oxford: the Cambridge cox had forgotten his team's own colours [2]. That story is told as hearsay, and the book does not say who first told it [2].

sections.title: Neighbors
sections.body: Paterson files Eton blue in his list of blues, alongside Cambridge blue, Delft blue and [[royal-blue]] [3]. In our own list the closest relatives are [[cambridge-blue]], [[sky-blue]] and [[french-blue]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch used on this page, #96C8A2, is not a light blue: it measures lightness 76.3, chroma 27.7 and hue angle 150 degrees, which is a pale blue-green [4]. The dictionary's description and this screen color do not match, so read the swatch as one modern rendering of the name, not a school's official shade [1][4].
